name: layered-redraw
description: Incubation prototype for non-destructive semantic-layer artwork across vector, raster, and pixel workflows; canonical runtime capabilities are upstreamed to VULCA SDK as reviewed Effect Packs.

interface.shortDescription: Plan from RGB and depth, then redraw in editable layers.
interface.longDescription: Turn one or more RGB references, optional RGB-D or estimated relative depth, a planning prompt, and an art-direction conversation into artwork with 5–20 stable semantic layers. Raw reference evidence remains immutable while Guided mode offers reusable visual-system presets and Art Direction exposes composition through material. The workflow can compare RGB and depth, resolve semantic regions into a bounded layer plan, generate parameterized A/B/C proofs, and promote one locked direction before production while retaining masks, recoverable history, quality gates, hybrid sources, and OpenRaster round trips.
defaultPrompt: Interview me, then redraw this photo as editable SVG layers.
Use Guided mode and show me composition-first design presets for this photo.
Use Art Direction mode so I can control proportion, space, form, value, and colour.
Register this RGB source, estimate relative depth, and use my prompt to plan 8–12 semantic layers.
Pair this RGB image with its supplied depth map, then keep the subject independently editable.
Generate A/B/C parameterized design proofs, let me lock one, then promote it to production.
Use raster-layered mode to generate editable PNG layers from this photo.
Create GBA warm-narrative pixel art with editable semantic layers.
Open my layered project and change only the selected or masked layers.
